sink.note: modern java.util.regex (JDK 11/17/21) prunes classic (a+)+$ (0ms); (.*a){N} survives the optimizer and is super-polynomial in N.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The fix for CVE-2026-45367 added RegexTimeout protection to matches() in DSTU2016MAY/DSTU3/R4/R4B/R5, but the DSTU2 module was incompletely patched: replaceMatches() was updated while matches() (line 2462) still calls raw String.matches(sw) without any timeout.

build.strategy: maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17; `mvn dependency:copy-dependencies` pulls the REAL published ca.uhn.hapi.fhir:org.hl7.fhir.dstu2 (+ transitive org.hl7.fhir.utilities, gson, ucum) from Maven Central per profile via build-arg FHIR_VER (6.9.6/6.9.7/6.9.10). A tiny REAL Java HTTP service (harness/src/main/java/Server.java, com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) exposes POST /eval {expr,input} -> new FHIRPathEngine(null).evaluate(new StringType(input), expr) running SYNCHRONOUSLY in the handler thread -- the library's own FHIRPathEngine is the sink, NO source edits. This mirrors a real FHIR server evaluating untrusted FHIRPath. The oracle triggers it via an EXTERNAL HTTP request and measures server-side response latency.
build.host_safety: the ReDoS is observed as external HTTP latency with a 10s client read timeout (a hang is recorded as ~10000ms, never an unbounded host wait). Each container is cpus=1.0, mem_limit=1500m, stop_grace_period=2s. Because a catastrophic FHIRPath evaluation permanently wedges the CPU-bound handler thread (a running java.util.regex cannot be interrupted), the oracle measures every probe against a FRESH server (kill + up -d between probes) so a slow probe never poisons the next. Input is a tiny 251-char string; the blow-up is pure-CPU exponential backtracking, flat memory. The server warms up the FHIRPathEngine at startup so per-request latency reflects only the matches()/replaceMatches() compute.

measured_latency_ms._note: SERVER-SIDE latency of an EXTERNAL HTTP POST /eval (client round-trip, ms). Catastrophic = 10s HTTP read timeout (~10002ms). Guard-bounded = RegexTimeout ~500ms then PathEngineException.

notes: REBUILT 2026-07-15 to a REAL Java HTTP service (per HARD POLICY: no in-process library trigger). Built from the REAL published ca.uhn.hapi.fhir:org.hl7.fhir.dstu2 6.9.6/6.9.7/6.9.10 (Maven Central, no source edits) behind a com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer whose POST /eval evaluates a user FHIRPath expression via the library's OWN FHIRPathEngine, SYNCHRONOUSLY, so a catastrophic matches()/replaceMatches() regex hangs the HTTP response. Confirmed on real Docker (cpus=1.0, mem 1500m, fresh server per probe): original replaceMatches('(.*a){30}') over 'a'x250+'X' HANGS on V0 (HTTP 10s timeout) and is BOUNDED ~510ms (RegexTimeout->PathEngineException) on V1 & V2; residual matches('(.*a){30}') HANGS on V0 AND on V1 (INCOMPLETE FIX: DSTU2 matches() still raw), and is BOUNDED ~515ms on V2 (CVE-2026-55470 fix). benign matches('a+') ~4ms everywhere. Clean separation on V1: original 510ms (bounded) vs residual 10002ms (hang), residual V1/V2 ~19.4x. Same class/regex/module, sibling FHIRPath functions, distinct CVEs / distinct fixed versions (6.9.7 vs 6.9.10). See repro.log + gate_result.json + patch.diff.
